title: The first Ext of a quotient by a finitely generated ideal fits into a canonical short exact sequence with the Koszul homology and the Hom of the naive Koszul module
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a finitely generated ideal I = (f_1, ..., f_n), and an R-module N, and defines the explicit module H_1(N, f_bullet) as the quotient of the n-tuples satisfying the Koszul relations by those of the form (f_1 x, ..., f_n x); it asserts that for every N there is a canonical short exact sequence 0 -> Ext_R(R/I, N) -> H_1(N, f_bullet) -> Hom_R(K, N), where K is the module of the naive Koszul complex (source lines 24412-24427). The proof first records the convention that the Ext groups here are those of the category of modules as defined earlier (proof lines 24429-24432). It then computes Ext_R(R/I, N) by applying the six-term exact sequence to the short exact sequence 0 -> I -> R -> R/I -> 0 and using Ext_R(R, N) = 0, obtaining Ext_R(R/I, N) = Coker(N -> Hom(I, N)) (proof lines 24433-24440). The substantive second step uses the short exact sequence of the naive Koszul complex to produce a complex N -> Hom(M, N) -> Hom_R(K, N) whose middle homology is canonically isomorphic to Ext_R(R/I, N) (proof lines 24441-24448). Since the cokernel of the first map of that complex is canonically isomorphic to H_1(N, f_bullet), the displayed short exact sequence follows and the proof is complete (proof lines 24448-24450). The non-routine content is the identification of Ext_R(R/I, N) with the middle homology of the explicit three-term complex, which is what places it in the displayed sequence.
